title: NASA Discovers Interstellar Comet Moving Through Solar System
text: The ATLAS survey telescope in Rio Hurtado, Chile reported the object on July 1, 2025; its hyperbolic path marks it as only the third known interstellar object.

title: Newly discovered interstellar object 'may be oldest comet ever seen'
text: Oxford researchers' population model suggests 3I/ATLAS likely comes from the Milky Way's ancient thick disk and could be older than the Solar System.

title: From a Different Star: 3I/ATLAS in the Context of the Ōtautahi–Oxford Interstellar Object Population Model
text: Paper estimates an age over 7.6 billion years (68% range ~7.6–14 Gyr) and predicts a water-rich, thick-disk origin.

title: 3I/Atlas: Mystery interstellar object could be the oldest known comet
text: Mainstream coverage of the 'oldest comet' estimate, possibly billions of years older than our Sun.

title: Is the Interstellar Object 3I/ATLAS Alien Technology?
text: A deliberately speculative paper flagging its retrograde orbit aligned within ~5° of the ecliptic and close planetary passes as possible technosignature 'anomalies'. Most astronomers treat 3I/ATLAS as a natural comet.

title: As NASA Missions Study Interstellar Comet, Hubble Makes Size Estimate
text: Hubble's July 21 images show a teardrop-shaped dust cocoon; nucleus is at most ~5.6 km wide and could be as small as ~440 m.

title: NASA's Webb Space Telescope Observes Interstellar Comet
text: JWST NIRSpec found a coma dominated by carbon dioxide, with a CO2/H2O ratio (~7.6) among the highest ever seen in a comet.

title: NASA's New SPHEREx Mission Observes Interstellar Comet
text: SPHEREx (Aug 8–12) detected an extended CO2 gas coma and water ice, when the comet was ~470 million km from the Sun.

title: VLT Observations of 3I/ATLAS II: Dramatic Rise of Ni I Emission
text: Nickel emission detected while iron was not, at distances where metals shouldn't sublimate — an unusual chemistry clue.

title: Extreme NiI/FeI abundance ratio in the coma of 3I/ATLAS
text: Measured nickel-to-iron ratio far above that of Solar System comets and of 2I/Borisov.

title: ESA's ExoMars and Mars Express observe Comet 3I/ATLAS
text: During its Oct 3 closest approach to Mars (~30 million km), ExoMars TGO's CaSSIS camera imaged the comet's coma.

title: Rapid Brightening of 3I/ATLAS Ahead of Perihelion
text: Solar coronagraphs (STEREO, SOHO, GOES-19) showed brightness rising as r^-7.5 near the Sun, and a coma bluer than the Sun.

title: Comet 3I/ATLAS Perihelion Update
text: An unexpected surge in brightness before solar conjunction; non-gravitational 'thruster-like' outgassing is being tracked.

title: No, interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS hasn't 'changed color', scientist says
text: A study author pushes back on viral 'color change' headlines: the gas coma made it look bluer, not a mysterious transformation.

title: NASA's Mars Spacecraft Capture Images of Comet 3I/ATLAS
text: MRO, MAVEN and Perseverance imaged the comet from Mars — the closest vantage of any NASA asset.

title: NASA's STEREO Observes Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS
text: STEREO tracked the comet Sept 11–Oct 2 while it was hidden behind the Sun from Earth.

title: NASA's PUNCH Spies Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS
text: Stacked PUNCH images reveal the comet's tail as a short elongation.

title: NASA-ESA's SOHO Observes Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS
text: SOHO's LASCO C3 coronagraph caught the comet Oct 15–26 near perihelion.

title: NASA's Lucy Spacecraft Snaps Photos of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS
text: Lucy imaged the comet and its tail from ~240 million miles away in mid-September.

title: NASA's Psyche Mission Tracks Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS
text: Four observations over eight hours on Sept 8–9 from ~53 million km helped refine the orbit.

title: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope Revisits Interstellar Comet
text: Hubble re-imaged the comet on Nov 30 from ~286 million km after it emerged from behind the Sun.

title: Determination of the Non-gravitational Accelerations of 3I/ATLAS
text: Spacecraft astrometry shows significant non-gravitational acceleration in all three axes, peaking ~35 days before perihelion — a 'course change' consistent with outgassing; implies mass ~44 million tons, radius ≲374 m.

title: Jets in the inner coma of comet 3I/ATLAS
text: Hubble Nov 30 data show a sunward anti-tail plus six faint straight jets in symmetric pairs. (Exact ATel posting day not verified; placed mid-Dec 2025.)

title: NASA's Europa Clipper Observes Comet 3I/ATLAS
text: Europa-UVS observed the comet on Nov 6 from ~164 million km in ultraviolet light.

title: NASA's Parker Solar Probe Observes Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS
text: WISPR took ~10 images a day Oct 18–Nov 5 as the comet swung around the Sun.

title: Anti-tail and nucleus-size constraints for 3I/ATLAS
text: Analyzes the tightly collimated sunward 'anti-tail' and compiles nucleus-size estimates from ~0.5 km to several km.

title: NASA's TESS Reobserves Comet 3I/ATLAS
text: Special TESS run Jan 15–22 to study the comet's activity and rotation.

title: NASA's SPHEREx Mission Tracks Brightening of Interstellar Comet
text: December 2025 infrared maps show the coma brightened in dust, water, organics and CO2 after perihelion.

title: First glimpse of Comet 3I/ATLAS from Juice science camera
text: JANUS image from Nov 6, 2025 shows coma, a long tail and hints of rays, jets and filaments. (Published Feb 2026; day approximate.)

title: Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS Data
text: More than a dozen NASA missions' 3I/ATLAS data are being archived publicly for future research.

title: NASA's Webb Detects Methane on Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS
text: Webb's first mid-infrared chemical fingerprint of an interstellar object reveals methane.

title: NASA's Webb Finds Clues to Ancient, Distant Origin of Comet 3I/ATLAS
text: December 2025 Webb measurements of H2O, CO2 and CO comas give chemical clues to an ancient, distant birthplace.

title: Near-perihelion Activity and Composition of 3I/ATLAS from JUICE/MAJIS
text: Juice saw water production fall from 8e28 to 4e28 molecules/s in Nov 2025, CO2 driving activity, and tentative complex organics.
